label: CFI
title: Cool Flames Investigation
hardware: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA), Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
tier_reason: Team list, Tier 2. PSI subarea: Droplets.

summary_student.text: Small drops of liquid fuel, such as n-dodecane, were burned inside a combustion chamber on the International Space Station. The study looked at cool flames, very weak flames that burn at low temperature and can keep going after a normal flame goes out. Understanding them helps explain how fuels ignite and supports the design of safer spacecraft.

summary_professional.text: Fiber-tethered or needle-suspended droplets of n-dodecane, farnesane and n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures were hot-wire ignited in the MDCA inside the CIR, in gas mixtures with helium dilution. The objective states pressures from 0.25 atm to 5 atm, while the approach states chamber pressures from 0.25 to 0.5 atm. A black-and-white camera measured droplet size, a UV camera captured OH* emission and flame size, and narrow-band and wide-band radiometers measured flame radiation. Targets were cool-flame behavior, droplet extinction diameters, flame dynamics and soot formation.

pillar.reason: The work characterizes low-temperature ignition and cool-flame extinction of liquid fuels, which informs how fuels can ignite and keep burning; the record links it to the design of safer spacecraft systems.

environments.reason: The tests were flown on the International Space Station in the Combustion Integrated Rack.
